bugs.title: A failed build never releases the build lock
bugs.body:
Observed by Rowan in run 20260907T015318Z, the first run on the diagonal tier, and verified in the guard source; the run was stopped with STOP after three attempts because every later attempt would pay the same cost.

WHAT HAPPENS. harness/src/harness/guard.gleam produces ReleaseBuild only in the "PostToolUse" branch of decide_input, and the generated settings register only a PostToolUse hook for Bash. Claude Code fires PostToolUse only when the tool call succeeds; a Bash call that exits nonzero fires PostToolUseFailure, which the guard never registered. A `lake build` that fails to compile — the normal case in the middle of a proof — therefore never releases the build lock. The lock stays held until its holder's next SUCCESSFUL build, and every sibling's `lake build` waits the full 240 s and is then denied with "build lock timeout".

TIMELINE. periodicFrom_mul's worker acquired the lock at 01:53:39; its build failed; no release. rightDiagonal_recurrence was denied at 01:58:04 and bool_xor_driven_periodicFrom at 02:00:29, both after 240 s. The holder's own next two builds each waited exactly 240 s (01:57:39, 02:01:39). The first release is logged at 02:01:43, after the holder's first successful build. At 02:01:43 rightDiagonal_recurrence acquired, its build failed, and the lock was stuck again. Last night's runs did not show it because every node closed on its first build.

WHY IT MATTERS. Three workers at concurrency 3 spent most of ten minutes waiting on one another. Each denial also costs the waiting worker a turn and a retry, so the stall reads later as budget_exhausted on a node it had nothing to do with (see harness-caused-abandonment-is-scored-as-difficulty).

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. (1) Register the same hook command under PostToolUseFailure with matcher Bash and treat it identically to PostToolUse in decide_input, so a failed build releases. (2) Defensively, on any PreToolUse from the current holder that is not itself an AcquireBuild, release the lock: a holder issuing a new tool call cannot still be building, so a missed hook can never hold the lock past the worker's next action. Test: a build that exits 1 must be followed by a release event, and a sibling's acquire must then succeed within seconds.

COST, FULL RUN (added after the run ended at 02:26:37Z). All three attempts closed proved: Vesper 15 turns, Cadence 28 turns, Selvage 22 turns, $1.47. Wall clock 33 minutes for three nodes whose actual proving fit in the first few minutes. Cadence held the lock through six failed builds (02:01:43, 02:05:43, 02:09:52, 02:13:52, 02:17:52, 02:21:52) and paid the full 240 s itself before each one, since its own stale hold had to time out before the re-acquire; the seventh build succeeded at 02:25:52 and released. Selvage was denied seven times (02:00:29 to 02:25:07), never built once in 30 minutes, then acquired within a second of Cadence's release and closed on its first build in 3 s. Selvage filed the same defect from inside as lake-build-repeatedly-hit-build-lock-timeout-despite; close both against one fix. Keel's fix is 24793a4 on keel/lock-timeout-verdict.
bugs.resolution: 24793a4 (Keel), landed in 6b239be. Premise confirmed in code: ReleaseBuild was produced only in the PostToolUse arm of decide_input and the generated settings registered Bash hooks under PreToolUse and PostToolUse only; PostToolUseFailure appeared nowhere. Two parts: the same hook command is now registered under PostToolUseFailure for Bash (settings_json and hooks/settings.template.json) and decide_input treats it exactly like PostToolUse for release, reading only tool_name and tool_input; and defensively, on any PreToolUse from the current holder that is not itself a build-acquiring call, the guard releases a stale hold first (lock.release_if_holding, which never withdraws a queued request) and writes a kind=lock row saying so, so a missed hook can never hold the lock past the worker's next action. Tests drive the real hook endpoint: a failed build is followed by a release and a sibling's acquire then succeeds; a holder's next non-build call releases; a second build does not release in front of its own acquire; the generated settings carry the new entry. Residual, documented: a worker that runs a build and another hooked call in parallel in one turn releases the running build's hold at the second call.

bugs.title: The test suite's STOP fixture halts a live run
bugs.body:
Observed by Keel on 2026-09-07 reading harness/test/run_test.gleam while Rowan's run was starting; not yet triggered, and it must not be, because triggering it costs a run.

WHAT HAPPENS. The stop-file test writes `f.cfg.repo_root <> "/STOP"` and deletes it a moment later. The fixture's cfg is `config.load()` with only dag_path, bugs_path, runs_root, roster_path and agents_dir redirected to a temp dir; repo_root is left as the live checkout, because that is where `.lake` is. So every `gleam test`, from any worktree, briefly creates C:/Users/dibuj/dev/rule30/STOP — which is exactly the captain's stop file, and the dispatcher checks it before every attempt it starts. A suite run during a live run can halt that run at any attempt boundary, and the run's log will say "stopped by STOP" with no one having asked for a stop. The same fixture root means verify_test's fixture proofs are written under the live Rule30/Proofs/ and built with a `lake build` there, outside the run's build lock, contending with live workers' builds.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, ONE OF THEM ALREADY COSTLY. Two suites at once can trip each other on STOP, a spurious failure. A suite during a run can end the run, which is not spurious: an attempt boundary is when the file is checked, so the window is small and the outcome is a halted run whose record looks like a deliberate stop.

RELATED. This is the sharpest instance of `offline-fixtures-write-into-the-live-checkout`, filed separately because that row is about fixtures leaving litter and this one is about a fixture that is a live control signal. CLAUDE.md already says never to run `gleam test` from a worktree during a run; this row says why that sentence is load-bearing, and that the rule exists only in prose.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. Cheapest: the stop test writes STOP under a per-fixture root rather than repo_root, which needs the dispatcher's stop-file path to be a config field (`stop_path`, defaulting to repo_root/STOP) that the fixture redirects like the other five. Then a suite cannot halt a run by construction, and verify_test's proof fixtures remain the only live-checkout writes, covered by the existing row.
bugs.resolution: fc0c096 (Keel), landed in 3aa8d97. The dispatcher's stop-file path became a config field, config.stop_path, defaulting to repo_root/STOP, and dispatch.fill reads that field and nothing else. run_test's fixture redirects it into the fixture's own directory alongside the other five redirected paths, so the stop test writes and deletes its STOP under harness/build/test-runs/ rather than at the root of the live checkout. Closure tests: config_test pins the default; a new run_test case runs a stopped fixture whose repo_root is the live checkout and asserts the halt reason names the fixture's own path and that the live checkout's STOP is in the same state after the run as before. Premise held at f41bd09 (dispatch.gleam:366-404, run_test.gleam:471,485). Audit found no other control-signal writes into repo_root; the proof fixtures remain under offline-fixtures-write-into-the-live-checkout.

bugs.title: A UserPromptSubmit hook that exits 2 blocks every prompt in every session in the checkout
bugs.body:
Filed by Keel on 2026-09-07 at Rowan's request, after causing it.

WHAT HAPPENED. b8f650c added a project-level UserPromptSubmit hook (.claude/hooks/session-title.sh) that returns the session's identity as its title. After its dry run passed, one more edit put a comment containing an apostrophe ("session's") inside the single-quoted Python block of the shell script. The apostrophe ended the shell string; bash hit a syntax error and exited 2. Claude Code treats exit 2 from a UserPromptSubmit hook as BLOCK THE PROMPT, so every prompt in every session running in the shared checkout was refused with the hook's stderr as the reason, including cross-session messages and task notifications, until Dib renamed the file by hand. Rowan lost one review report to it.

THE MECHANISM, for the next person who writes a hook here. Project settings (.claude/settings.json) apply to every session whose working directory is the checkout: hand-started overseers and framework agents, and dispatched workers too. A UserPromptSubmit hook runs before every prompt is accepted. Exit 0 with JSON on stdout is honoured; any non-zero exit other than 2 is shown as a non-blocking error; exit 2 blocks the prompt and shows stderr. A shell syntax error is exit 2. So a hook script with any quoting hazard in it can, by a one-character edit, stop every session in the repository from receiving input, and the failure reaches every peer before it reaches the author.

WHY THE TEST DID NOT CATCH IT. The dry run was of the file before the last edit. The artifact shipped was not the artifact tested; the same failure as quoting from memory instead of from git show, one column over.

THE FIX (ab99010). The Python moved into its own file, .claude/hooks/session-title.py, where no shell quoting can reach it; the wrapper is three lines that exit 0 on every path; and the cases registered, unknown session, garbage stdin, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset and a deliberately broken Python file were each run after the final edit and each exited 0.

THE RULE. A hook that can block a peer's prompt must be unable to fail loudly by construction: keep the shell wrapper too small to break, put logic in a file the shell never parses, exit 0 on every path, and run the dry run on the file you commit, not the one you tested a minute earlier. Never edit .claude/ while a run is in flight, for the same reason multiplied by every worker.
bugs.resolution: ab99010 (Keel). The Python moved into .claude/hooks/session-title.py where no shell quoting can reach it; the wrapper is three lines that exit 0 on every path; registered, unknown, garbage-stdin, no-CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and deliberately-broken-Python cases were run after the final edit and each exited 0. Verified live: Rowan's session retitled to Rowan on its next prompt with no error. Filed after the fix, at Rowan's request, so the mechanism is on the board for the next hook author.

bugs.title: gleam run -- writes does not list a declared writer whose call sits in a Gleam match arm
bugs.body:
Filed by Fathom on 2026-09-07, from the final review of the theorem index (landed a96016c).

WHAT HAPPENED. writes.gleam declares blueprint/index.md with writers ["write_in", "index.write"] and its risk line names `gleam run -- index` as a writer. bugs.title: Cast arithmetic between ℕ, ℤ and ℝ eats prover budgets on two-line facts
bugs.body:
Observed by Rowan across the 2026-09-07 runs; Dib asked what could be built. Three budget_exhausted attempts today, and two of them were casts.

EVIDENCE. runs/20260907T164112Z/centerColumnCount_sandwich-1 (haiku, 41 turns, $0.63): 15 builds, the same `omega could not prove the goal` at line 30 ten times, 325 mentions of push_cast/zify/omega in the transcript; the statement is a two-line induction and closed on sonnet in 9 turns. runs/20260907T164112Z/centerColumn_excess_interpolate-1 (sonnet, 41 turns, $1.36): the statement mixes a ℕ count, a ℤ difference and an absolute value; `Unknown identifier abs_add` twice (a Mathlib name that has drifted), 133 cast-tactic mentions; closed on opus in 9 turns. Earlier the same day the provers' notebooks on the diagonal tier all say the same thing in their own words: `most of the proof is omega/push_cast bookkeeping` (Vesper), `cast normalizations require push_cast; omega` (Cadence). runs/20260907T161211Z/rule30_left_local_law-1 was NOT casts (rewrite failures on Bool), included here as the control.

WHY IT MATTERS. Size M on this board currently means `has a cast in it`, not `has an idea in it`. The ladder pays a rung, sometimes two, for arithmetic a mathematician would not write down, and the cost lands on exactly the nodes P2 needs most, because counts are ℕ, excesses are ℤ and the prize is ℝ.

WHAT WOULD HELP, in order of cost. (1) Statement design, captain side, no code: prefer ℕ statements; an absolute value over casts can almost always be two ℕ inequalities (the interpolation node is `count N - count M ≤ N - M` and `count M ≤ count N` in ℕ); the seeder brief's proposal-format section should say so, and the seed check could warn when an elaborated statement contains `Nat.cast`, `Int.cast` or `abs` (a count of those three in the checked type is enough). (2) A cast cookbook paragraph in the prover brief, brief.gleam: the `zify`/`push_cast`/`omega` pattern for ℕ-to-ℤ goals, `Nat.cast_sub` needs its `≤` hypothesis, `Int.natAbs` and `abs_le` for absolute values, and one sentence saying Mathlib lemma names drift, so `#check` a name before building on it (Selvage and the interpolation worker both lost turns to a guessed name). (3) A served module Rule30/Casts.lean carrying the five or six cast lemmas provers keep re-deriving, once two attempts have re-derived the same one; not yet. (4) Measurement, outcome-scoring side: an attempt whose transcript repeats the same `omega could not prove` line more than three times is cast-cycling, and the auto-filed friction row could say so, so this stops being an impression.

DOES NOT ASK for a wider guard, a bigger budget, or a tactic the toolchain lacks.
bugs.resolution: 9b0d4a0 (Keel), landed in dfa9f4a, for the brief half: every prover brief carries docs/prover-cookbook.md whole, read from disk at render time, under the heading 'Casts and names, checked against this pin', placed after the constraints and before the served lemmas, with a one-line absence notice if the file is missing; a test reads the real file and pins the placement. Evidence the row records: two of the three budget exhaustions on 2026-09-07 were cast cycling and both facts closed in nine turns one rung up. The lower-priority half, a seed-check warning when an elaborated statement contains Nat.cast, Int.cast or abs, is not in this landing and is Keel's next small change in seed.gleam; the next runs' budget-exhaustion causes are the test of the brief half.

bugs.title: The board does not record which wall a block was seeded to attack
bugs.body:
Found by Fathom's index final review on 2026-09-07: the index's 'the wall it sits under' clause is computed as 'walls whose transitive deps reach this node' and renders on zero of 64 nodes, because walls carry deps: [] and nothing lists a wall as a dependent. The code is right about the relation it computes; the board never records the relation it wanted.

WHY deps IS THE WRONG PLACE. deps means 'must be proved before this node is dispatched' and the scheduler reads it that way; a wall is never dispatched, and giving it deps would assert a proof route that does not exist. 'Decomposes' is a different relation: 'this block was seeded as part of attacking that wall', set by the captain at landing, the way object is.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. A captain-set field `under: <wall id>` on dag.Node, optional, encoded only when present and round-tripped unvalidated (exactly as object was added in 43cf4aa), plus the index renderer reading `under` instead of the transitive-deps computation. Today it is non-empty on the five nodes of the first seeder tier (under leftDiagonal_period_le) and empty elsewhere; the seeder's proposal format could carry it so a proposal names the wall it attacks. Until it exists the index says the clause is knowingly empty.
bugs.resolution: 4d5c8e3 (Keel), landed in 0e61dcf. dag.Node gained under: Option(String), the id of the wall a block was seeded to attack, captain-set at landing exactly as object is: never set or checked by the harness, decoded as None when absent, encoded only when present, so a run's save writes back what the captain wrote. The seeder's proposal format gained the same optional under; the brief tells a seeder to name the wall it attacks when it attacks one, and the check report prints it on its own line. The index's 'under the wall' clause now reads node.under, printed by the wall's lean_name when the id names a node and verbatim otherwise, omitted when absent; the transitive-deps computation is deleted with a comment recording why deps could never carry this relation. The board was not edited: the clause renders on no node until the captain sets the field, and the five first-tier blocks under leftDiagonal_period_le are the first candidates.

bugs.title: A theorist session runs under the prover's 40-turn, $4 ceilings
bugs.body:
Observed by Rowan on 2026-09-07 in run 20260907T175146Z, the first theorist session (persona Sextant, fable, topic the P1 frontier wall): 13 turns in about seven minutes, $4.27, summary 'the CLI ended the session' with stop_reason tool_use, ending recorded as budget exhausted, no structured report. Cause confirmed by Keel in code, not from the summary: theorist.gleam:735 calls worker.launch(cfg, ...) with the run's config unchanged, so the session runs under cfg.max_turns (HARNESS_MAX_TURNS, 40) and cfg.max_budget_usd (HARNESS_MAX_BUDGET_USD, 4.0), the prover's ceilings; $4.27 against a $4.00 cap says the dollar ceiling is what ended it. seeder.gleam:296 has the same shape and has only survived because a seeder has been cheap.

WHY IT MATTERS. The connections spec, Piece 4, says a theorist's budget is hours, not turns, and that its cost is expected to exceed a seeder's by an order of magnitude; that is the point of the role. A theorist capped like a prover produces a truncated document with no report, and the truncation reads in the record as budget exhaustion, which is the prover's word for a hard node. The first theorist document is therefore not evidence about the topic.

THE FIX. Ceilings of their own: HARNESS_THEORIST_MAX_TURNS and HARNESS_THEORIST_MAX_BUDGET_USD (defaults 600 and 80.0), HARNESS_SEEDER_MAX_TURNS and HARNESS_SEEDER_MAX_BUDGET_USD (80 and 12.0), applied in theorist.run and seeder.run before the launch the way config.for_attempt applies the research ceilings, recorded in the session's dispatch event and printed in the summary. In progress on keel/theorist-budget.
bugs.resolution: b2a6763 (Keel), landed in 2ad28f9. theorist.run and seeder.run handed worker.launch the run's config unchanged, so a theorist ran under HARNESS_MAX_TURNS 40 and HARNESS_MAX_BUDGET_USD 4.0; Sextant (run 20260907T175146Z) ended at error_max_budget_usd, 'Reached maximum budget ($4)', thirteen turns in, with no report and a half-written document. Config gained theorist_max_turns and theorist_max_budget_usd (600, 80.0) and seeder_max_turns and seeder_max_budget_usd (80, 12.0), each with a HARNESS_* override, and for_theorist and for_seeder mirroring for_attempt; both verbs apply theirs before launch, record the pair in the dispatch event under the prover's field names, and print a ceilings line in the summary. Tests observe the shim's actual --max-turns and --max-budget-usd. The summary cannot yet say which ceiling ended a session (worker.End does not distinguish and claude.gleam does not decode the result subtype), so it says 'a ceiling' and the notes carry the CLI's own result line; that split is a separate small row if anyone wants it.

bugs.title: A structured report sent in the CLI's last turn is dropped when the result is an error
bugs.body: Observed by Rowan on 2026-09-07 in run 20260907T175146Z (Sextant, fable). The session's last assistant turn called StructuredOutput with outcome attacked, summary, notebook (1877 chars), journal (1068 chars) and next_topic; the CLI's result event for that turn has subtype error_max_budget_usd, is_error true, errors ['Reached maximum budget ($4)'] and no structured_output field. worker.gleam (the is_error arm around line 905) decodes the report only from the result's structured_output, so the harness recorded 'no report', ended as budget_exhausted, wrote no notebook entry and no journal entry, and the summary said '(no report, so no next topic)'. The report's text survives only as the tool_use input in the stream events. Rowan wrote Sextant's notebook and journal entries by hand from it this once. Suggested fix: when the result carries no structured_output, recover the last StructuredOutput tool_use input from the turn's own stream events before concluding there was no report; the ceiling that ended the session is a separate fact from whether the session reported.
bugs.resolution: 4d303cc (Keel), landed in 2ad28f9. The CLI copies a session's StructuredOutput call into the turn's result as structured_output, except when that same result ends the session in error, when it carries no copy at all; the turn loop read only the result, so Sextant's complete final report was recorded as 'no report' and no notebook or journal was written. The loop now falls back to the last StructuredOutput call in the turn's own stream (an assistant event's tool_use block named StructuredOutput), decodes it with the role's own decoder, logs report_recovered, and proceeds as if the result had carried it; a call that fails to decode logs report_recovery_failed rather than vanishing; a turn with no such call is unchanged. Holds for every role driven by worker.drive. Sextant's own report is not recovered retroactively; Rowan wrote its notebook and journal by hand from the events.

bugs.title: The theorist guard makes nothing under explorer/ writable, but the spec and the task text both ask for falsification scripts there
bugs.body: Observed by Rowan on 2026-09-07 from Sextant's attack document and notebook (run 20260907T175146Z): 'I assumed I could write scripts under explorer/ as the theorist brief says; the fence forbade it and allowed only bare node <existing script>, so my only engine reading was diagonalscan.mjs at its defaults'. No denial was logged: the brief's fence paragraph (theorist.gleam around line 565, 'no script under explorer/ (put a script's text in the document)') told it not to try, so every falsification in the document was done by pencil and the scripts are quoted as text. Three texts disagree. docs/theorist-brief.md lines 37-40: 'write a script under explorer/, run it with node explorer/<file>.mjs'. The connections design spec, Piece 4, Fence: 'The seeder's guard with two changes: no write access to blueprint/proposals/next.json, and write access to exactly one new file, docs/attacks/<date>-<topic>.md, plus append access to docs/obstructions.md' — the seeder's guard makes anything under explorer/ writable (guard.gleam line 68), so the spec keeps it. guard.gleam lines 86-87 drop it: 'Nothing under explorer/ is writable: a theorist's deliverable is an argument'. Rowan's ruling as the spec's author: the spec stands; a theorist writes under explorer/ exactly as a seeder does, because falsification by script is the role's first discipline and the deliverable rule is about statements and proposals, not scripts. This is a widening of the guard, and CLAUDE.md says a widening is never a fix on its own: the reason it is one here is that the guard contradicts the spec it implements, not that a correct denial was inconvenient.
bugs.resolution: a397700 (Keel), landed in 2ad28f9. The spec defines the theorist's guard as the seeder's with two changes, and the seeder's guard makes explorer/ writable; guard.gleam's Theorist arm had dropped it and the brief said so in words, which is why Sextant did its falsification by pencil under a brief demanding an engine run per claim. The Theorist write arm now carries the seeder's under_explorer clause beside the two named files, with the same dot-dot refusal and separator check so explorer/../Rule30/Statements.lean stays denied; the brief says scripts under explorer/ may be written freely. next.json, Statements.lean, dag.json, crystals.md and agents/ remain denied, each tested. This restores the spec's fence rather than widening past it.

bugs.title: Two theorist sessions on the same topic on the same day resolve to the same attack file, which the second may overwrite
bugs.body: Observed by Rowan on 2026-09-07 before starting Sextant's second session. theorist.gleam attack_path builds docs/attacks/<date>-<slug(topic)>.md from today's date and the topic alone, and the guard's Theorist role allows writes to exactly that path. So a second session on the same topic on the same day is fenced to the file the first session wrote, and its Write overwrites the first document; the design's intended use ('several independent sessions on one topic, then a comparison') is the case that collides. Worked around by extending the topic text so the slug differs. Suggested fix: include the run id or a per-day counter in the file name when the path already exists, or refuse to start with the reason, and never fence a theorist to a file that exists.
bugs.resolution: 7ba4dcc (Keel), landed in 5fada35. theorist.run chooses the attack path once at session start with free_attack_path: the bare <date>-<slug>.md when nothing is there, else -2.md, -3.md, the first free, with anything at the path counting as taken. The guard's fence, the brief, the first message, the dispatch event's attack field and the summary all carry that one path, so a second session on a topic in one day is fenced to its own file and the guard denies the first session's. Tested end to end with the first document on disk: the second lands on the -2 file and the first is unchanged afterwards.

bugs.title: A session ended by the CLI is recorded as budget exhausted whether turns or dollars ran out
bugs.body:
Found by Keel while fixing a-theorist-runs-under-a-provers-ceilings on 2026-09-07; Rowan asked for the row.

WHAT HAPPENS. worker.End.BudgetExhausted covers three endings: the CLI ended the session at its turn ceiling (result subtype error_max_turns), the CLI ended it at its dollar ceiling (subtype error_max_budget_usd), and the harness's own round budget (cfg.max_verify_rounds) ran out. claude.gleam's result decoder reads is_error and the errors list but not subtype, so the turn loop never sees which. A theorist's or seeder's summary therefore says 'stopped at a ceiling' and points at the notes, which carry the CLI's raw result line; a prover's attempt is recorded as budget_exhausted with the same ambiguity, and the ladder and the scorecard treat all three alike.

WHY IT MATTERS. Sextant's first session (run 20260907T175146Z) ended at error_max_budget_usd after 13 turns; a reader of summary.txt could not tell that from a 600-turn session that talked itself out, and the fix for one (a bigger dollar ceiling) is not the fix for the other (a brief that ends the loop). The scorecard's calibration reads a budget exhaustion as the node's difficulty; a dollar ceiling hit by an expensive brief is not that.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. Decode subtype in claude.gleam's TurnResult; carry it into worker.End as a reason (turns, dollars, rounds); name it in the ending notes, the summary's ended line and the attempt's outcome notes. Optionally, an attempt ended by the dollar ceiling below the turn ceiling is scored like HarnessFailed rather than difficulty, since the ceiling and not the node ended it. Small.
bugs.resolution: f8d92c1 (Keel), landed in 5fada35. claude.gleam's result decoder now reads the CLI's subtype into TurnResult, and worker.End's BudgetExhausted carries a Ceiling (Turns, Dollars, Rounds, or Unknown with the subtype verbatim) derived from the subtype when the CLI ended the session and fixed at Rounds when the harness's round budget did. The ending's notes open with the ceiling and its value from the config the session ran under, which is what a prover's attempt records; the theorist's and seeder's summary ended line reads 'stopped at the CLI's dollar ceiling ($80.0)', 'stopped at the CLI's turn ceiling (600 turns)' or 'stopped at the harness's round budget (4 rounds)'; a theorist's notebook heading says budget_exhausted: dollars. dag.Outcome is unchanged and scoring is untouched: the optional idea of scoring a dollar-ceiling ending like HarnessFailed is left for a decision, with the reason now in the notes for whoever makes it.

bugs.title: seed.check_declaration writes one scratch file per lean_name with no per-call token, and the automatic proposal check is now a second producer
bugs.body:
Filed by Fathom on 2026-09-07 from the final review of the worker-proposals landing.

WHAT HAPPENED. seed.gleam's check_declaration writes <repo_root>/harness/build/checks/seed/<lean_name>.lean and elaborates it, with the path derived from the lean_name alone. run_witness, right beside it, takes a per-call token for exactly the reason its own comment gives: two sessions on this machine share one checkout, and a path derived only from the node name is one absolute path with no lock on it (four spurious failures on 2026-09-06). Until the proposals landing that path had one producer, a hand-started `seed check`. The dispatcher now runs seed.check_file_in automatically at the end of every run (and at the end of every prove-one) over the attempt's proposals.json, and a seeder is designed to run beside a run, so two checks of the same lean_name can now race on the same file.

WHY IT MATTERS. A collision here is a spurious RouteFailed on a route that closes, reported in the captain's check report as a verdict about the statement.

CLOSURE TEST. check_declaration's scratch file carries a per-call token the way run_witness's does (grep seed.gleam for the token in run_witness and mirror it), and a test in seed_test that two concurrent check_declaration calls on one lean_name write two files.
bugs.resolution: 6d9fb9e (Keel), landed in d405573. The premise held for the route check only: check_declaration named its scratch file by lean_name alone and never removed it, while run_witness (seed.gleam:531, which the row cited as tokenless) already carried a per-call token but also left its file behind, so the collision was real on the route side and the litter on both. Both checks now go through one helper that names the file <stem>_<32 hex from harness_ffi.token>.lean, deletes it after the check on the path this call wrote and never another's, and reports a failed delete to stderr without touching the verdict. Tests pin that two checks of one statement never share a path, the token's shape, and that a failed route, a closed route and a broken witness each leave nothing behind, with the failed cases recovering the path from Lean's own error output. Three producers exist, not two: the run-end check, seed check, and the seeder session's own check at its end. verify.gleam's check file (harness/build/checks/<node.id>.lean) has the same shape under a weaker premise (one attempt per claimed node, verifier under the build lock) and is left as is; a reopen beside a live run is the one way it could collide.

bugs.title: The startup skill says to message any live ref with no sessions.json row, and a live theorist is exactly that
bugs.body:
Filed by Fathom on 2026-09-07 after doing it, at 19:46:26Z, five minutes into session rule30-e7.

WHAT HAPPENED. /startup (Job 3) says a live ref with no row in agents/sessions.json is an unknown session and to message it and ask who it is. ListAgents showed rule30-bf [794019], no row, started 18m earlier. I messaged it. It was Rowan's live theorist in runs/20260907T192739Z/theorist-1, whose guard events run to 19:42Z and whose start matches the run's to the minute. The skill's Job 1 says dispatched provers are deliberately absent from the file because a message would reach a worker as an instruction from outside its brief; theorists and seeders are absent for the same reason, but the skill only names provers, and Job 3's rule does not say to check runs/ before messaging. So the skill's two halves, read together, instruct a new session to do the thing the Boundaries section calls the expensive failure. The arrival leaves no trace in the theorist's record, by the known limit workers-are-addressable-and-it-is-not-recorded; the only possible evidence is a guard denial if the theorist obeys the /startup I told it to run.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every hand-started session runs /startup first, so this is the first thing a fresh framework session does while a theorist or seeder is live, and a theorist is exactly the session whose output Dib reads as evidence about a topic.

CLOSURE TEST. state.sh prints, next to the registered-sessions table, every attempt directory under runs/ whose events.jsonl has a guard event within the last N minutes, labelled as a guarded session that must not be messaged; and the skill's Job 3 says to check that list before messaging an unknown ref, and says theorist and seeder sessions are absent from sessions.json on purpose. A test that a fixture run with a recent theorist-1 event makes the report name it.

EVIDENCE, added 19:55Z after Rowan read the record. Second instance of workers-are-addressable-and-it-is-not-recorded. runs/20260907T192739Z/theorist-1/events.jsonl line 14: at 19:47:17Z the theorist (Sextant) called SendMessage to my address and the guard denied it, not_permitted, "a dispatched session cannot message another session". That denial is the only trace the arrival left: one theorist turn spent answering a message it should never have received. No edit to sessions.json was attempted.
bugs.resolution: 6ad8648 (Fathom): state.sh lists attempts with an event in the last 30m and no summary.txt as live guarded sessions; SKILL.md Job 1 names theorists and seeders as absent by design, Job 3 says to match a rowless ref against that section before calling it unknown. Fixture with a 4m-old theorist event listed; ended seeder and 3h-old prover not; real runs/ empty after Sextant ended.

bugs.title: An abandoned or exhausted attempt leaves its worker's file under Rule30/Proofs/, where only closed nodes' files belong
bugs.body: Observed by Rowan on 2026-09-07 after run 20260907T201514Z: the opus attempt on leftDiagonal_onset_le ended abandoned and Rule30/Proofs/LeftDiagonalOnsetLe.lean stayed on disk, holding a different, proved lemma (leftDiagonal_step_onset_dichotomy) and no sorry. CLAUDE.md's layout rule is one file per closed node under Rule30/Proofs/, and the file was not imported by Proofs.lean, so the build was unaffected; but a captain committing the run's outputs with `git add -A Rule30/Proofs` swept it in (65cf7a8), and a later attempt on the same node starts from a file it did not write. Rowan moved it to explorer/scratch_onset_dichotomy.lean by hand. Suggested fix: when an attempt ends in any outcome but proved, move the worker's file into the attempt's directory under runs/<run>/<node>-<n>/ (keeping it as the attempt's record, which the worker's own report may cite), so Rule30/Proofs/ holds exactly the closed nodes' files at every moment between attempts. If the next attempt on a node should see the previous file, the brief can point at the attempt directory.
bugs.resolution: 5e8b6a4 (Fathom): moved, not left. An attempt ending in any outcome but Closed, or crashing, has its Rule30/Proofs/<Node>.lean moved into runs/<run>/<node>-<n>/ with a proof_file event and a summary line; the next brief on the node finds the parked file under runs/ and says to read it first and keep what builds, so Keel's 74d2a84 intent survives. Chosen over the fallback (leave it, list it in the summary) because the invariant Dib and captains rely on is what the directory contains, and a listing does not change that; a reader of Rule30/Proofs/ should not need the summary. Reads are not gated by the worker hook matcher, so no guard change. Closure: run_test moves a token-named probe out of the live directory into the attempt dir and a proved attempt keeps its file; brief tests cover the sentence and the runs/ lookup; 527 announced, 527 passed.

bugs.title: A live theorist or connector session cannot be observed: stream events are written at turn end and there is no human-readable live view
bugs.body: Dib, 2026-09-07 20:50Z, on Sextant's fourth session: 'I wish I could more easily observe what Sextant or a future connector are up to. They run for a long time.' What exists: the guard's PreToolUse lines in theorist-1/events.jsonl, live, which show tool calls and nothing else; the scripts it writes, readable on disk; the document, written in one Write near the end. What does not: worker.read_turn_loop collects every stream event of a turn in `seen` and turn_loop writes them to events.jsonl only when the TurnResult arrives (worker.gleam around lines 867-868), so a 36-minute turn with 36 tool calls has flushed zero assistant text, zero tool results, zero cost. Two parts to a fix. (1) Log each stream event as it arrives, in read_turn_loop's next(), and drop the batch write; the file is append-only and the order is unchanged. (2) A verb `gleam run -- watch <run-id> [<session>]` that tails the attempt's events.jsonl and renders one line per event a person would read: assistant text (first line), tool call (tool and the file or command), tool result (first line, is_error), guard denial with reason, and a running turn count and cost from the rate_limit/result events; theorist-1, connector-1, seed-1 and <node>-<n> alike. Until then the captain's substitute is `tail -f` on events.jsonl piped through grep for guard lines, which Dib should not have to know. Rowan is separately changing the theorist and connector briefs to write the document early and update it as they go, so there is a readable artifact mid-session.

bugs.title: An auto-filed signature whose last row is wontfix opens a fresh row every run
bugs.body:
Filed by Keel on 2026-09-07 while closing guard-denied-bash-not-permitted-5.

WHAT HAPPENED. bugs.append dedupes an auto-filed signature only against a live row (open or claimed, is_live in bugs.gleam). When the last row carrying the signature is closed, a new numbered row is opened, and the doc comment justifies that for one case only: 'a signature matching a bug already fixed files a new row, so a regression is visibly a regression'. It says nothing about wontfix, and the code treats the two alike. Result: guard:Bash:not_permitted has five rows in twenty-three hours, three of them closed wontfix with the same reasoning, each costing a framework agent a claim, a premise check and a resolution to say again that the denial was correct.

WHY IT MATTERS. Fixed and wontfix are opposite verdicts about recurrence. After a fix, one more occurrence is news (a regression) and deserves a fresh row. After a wontfix, recurrence is the expected behaviour the verdict described, and the useful record is the count, not a new question -- the -3 and -4 resolutions both say the occurrence count on later runs is the measure of whether the brief works, and today that measure is scattered over five rows. Same split as an error tracker's Resolved versus Ignored: a resolved issue reopens on the next event, an ignored one keeps counting and stays quiet.

CLOSURE TEST. A test in bugs_test that an append whose signature matches a row closed wontfix bumps that row's occurrences and filed and adds no row, while append_does_not_dedupe_against_a_fixed_bug_test still passes; and that a signature whose newest row is fixed, with an older wontfix behind it, still opens a fresh row.
bugs.resolution: b13f4fc (Keel): bugs.append now lets the newest row carrying a signature decide — bumped (occurrences and filed) unless that row is fixed, so a wontfix row absorbs its recurrences and stays off the open list while a fixed row still yields a fresh row for the regression. Closure test: bugs_test append_bumps_a_wontfix_row_instead_of_filing_a_new_one_test fails at f901d27 (pattern match on one row finds two) and passes at b13f4fc; append_does_not_dedupe_against_a_fixed_bug_test and the new newest-row-decides test pass at both. Suite 523 of 523 in the worktree, announced total matched. From the next run on, a not_permitted denial bumps guard-denied-bash-not-permitted-5 rather than opening a -6.

bugs.title: A CLI result of subtype success with no structured report ends an attempt as budget_exhausted, and counts as a ladder attempt
bugs.body: Observed by Rowan on 2026-09-07 in run 20260907T210826Z, attempt column_settledConfig_eq-1 (Vesper, opus): after three turns and $0.92 the CLI returned a result with subtype success, stop_reason stop_sequence, 295 output tokens and no structured_output; the notes read 'the CLI ended the session at a CLI ending this harness has no name for (result subtype success)' and the outcome was recorded as budget_exhausted. Sextant's theorist session in the same minute (20260907T210845Z) was parked as rate_limited by the five-hour window, so this ending was the rate limit arriving on a prover as a short empty success turn rather than as a rate_limit_event. Two consequences: the attempt now sits on the node's ladder as an exhausted opus rung, so the next dispatch skips a rung it never really used; and the naming fix's honest 'no name for' is exactly the case that should be treated as a pause, not a verdict. Suggested fix: a result with is_error false, no structured_output and a turn count far below the ceiling ends the attempt as RateLimited (parked, resumable) or at least as an outcome that does not advance the ladder; and the ending word should name it.
bugs.resolution: 62a3ddf (Fathom): not a naming bug — a decoder one. claude.gleam required unifiedWindows.five_hour.utilization as decode.float, and JSON writes exactly two utilization values without a decimal point, 0 and 1, so the decoder was blind at both ends of the range and nowhere else. A full window is the only reading that must park a run, and subfield being required meant the whole event was dropped to Other rather than one field misread: hit_ceiling never saw a RateLimit, the attempt ran on to the CLI's error result and was scored against the node's ladder. Measured over the attempt logs runs/*/*/events.jsonl (166 files, 774 rate-limit events; 803 including run-root logs, which hold none of the integers): six integers, of which u=0 allowed x4, u=0 allowed_warning x1, u=1 rejected x1 — that last being column_settledConfig_eq-1 in run 20260907T210826Z, the attempt that paid. Closure: a_full_window_parks_the_attempt_test drives the real recorded event through the loop and asserts dag.RateLimited; an_empty_window_does_not_park_the_attempt_test pins the other end, because 0 is an integer too and a fix that merely tolerated integers without status remaining the authority would have parked every session starting on a fresh window. Suite 649/649, exit 0.

bugs.title: A theorist or seeder parked by a rate limit prints 'resume session <id>' but no verb accepts it
bugs.body: Observed by Rowan on 2026-09-07: Sextant's fifth session (run 20260907T210845Z) ended 'rate limited' after three turns and $3.08 with the summary line 'the five-hour window is rate limiting; resume session 18e46aaf-a3af-4d38-8fc6-d6363b8b7205'. For provers a later `run` resumes a parked attempt by that session id (worker.gleam around line 1048); theorist.gleam and seeder.gleam park the same way but `theorise` and `seed` take no session id, so the only way to continue is a fresh session that has lost the parked one's context, and the document, if it was written early as the brief now asks, would be overwritten or collide. Suggested fix: `theorise --resume <session-id>` (and `seed --resume`) that relaunches the CLI with --resume on that id under the same guard, record directory and attack path, appending to the same events.jsonl with a `resumed` event; the summary's 'resume session' line then names the command.

bugs.title: Every hand-started session kind is a fresh copy of the same nine hundred lines
bugs.body:
Filed by Keel on 2026-09-07 at Dib's instruction, from the connector build.

WHAT IS TRUE AT HEAD. theorist.gleam is 989 lines and 32 functions; seeder.gleam is 378 lines and 11; eleven function NAMES already appear in both (default_port, ended_words, parse_flags, parse_flags_into, report_decoder, report_from_dynamic, report_schema, role, run, summary, task_message), and the bodies differ only in the role's words and paths. The connector was planned as a third copy: 59 percent of its implementation plan (1864 of 3161 lines, tasks 6 and 7) was a near-duplicate of theorist.gleam, against 825 lines for the only genuinely new thing in the role, its read-only web access. Dib saw the plan's size and asked why a role that is 'the theorist with a different prompt' costs ten tasks. That question is the bug.

WHY IT MATTERS. What is duplicated is not incidental: it is the naming ceremony, the report schema and its decoder, the turn loop, the channel writes, the summary and the ceilings -- the machinery that decides what a session IS. Three copies means a fix to any of it lands in one kind and silently not the others, and the harness has already had exactly that shape of bug: the theorist inherited a prover's config, fence and result decoder by default and all three were wrong for it (see the 19:10Z entry in agents/Keel.md, landed 2ad28f9). A fourth kind pays the whole cost again.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE. The connector's plan was cut down rather than executed as written: it reuses theorist.gleam's generic functions instead of copying them. AMENDED by Keel on 2026-09-08, because this row first called that a handful of functions and the rewrite measured otherwise: it takes SEVEN private functions made public (ensure_identity, who_you_are, inlined, document_size, ceilings, end_word, ended_words) and NINE parameterised (who, the document-path family of four, report_schema, who_you_are, end_word, ended_words), with the theorist's own call sites passing what they used to hardcode. connector.gleam came out a quarter smaller for it, 628 lines to 465. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE USEFUL PART OF THIS ROW: the hard half of the extraction, making those functions role-agnostic, is done on the connector branch, so what is left here is closer to a file move plus the same treatment for seeder.gleam. Read theorist.gleam at that landing before estimating from this body. It leaves connector.gleam importing theorist.gleam, which is honest but backwards.

WHAT THIS ROW ASKS FOR. Extract the generic spine into a module of its own that no session kind owns -- flags, the ceremony, the report schema and decoder, the run loop, the channels, the summary, the ceilings, the document path rules -- and leave theorist.gleam, seeder.gleam and connector.gleam holding only what actually differs: the brief, the fence, the paths, the report's words. Not to be done during a live run, and not while the connector branch is open.

CLOSURE TEST. No function name appears in more than one of theorist.gleam, seeder.gleam and connector.gleam; connector.gleam does not import theorist; the suite passes with its announced total; and a theorist, a seeder and a connector each still start, brief and summarise as they do today.

bugs.title: gleam test can die before the suite starts, printing something a worker will read as a failing test
bugs.body:
Observed by Keel on 2026-09-08 during the connector build, twice in one session, in the worktree rule30-keel-connector.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED. Two erl_crash.dump files were written into harness/ by suite runs. The first, 21:04Z, has slogan 'Kernel pid terminated (application_controller) ({application_terminated,kernel,shutdown})' -- a BEAM killed from outside, consistent with a subagent being cut off by a rate limit mid-run. The second, 01:58Z, is different and is the reason for this row: slogan 'Runtime terminating during boot ({badarg,[{erlang,display_string,["Error! Failed to eval: harness@@main:run(harness_test)

"]...' -- the runtime never reached the suite at all.

WHY IT MATTERS, AND IT IS NOT THE CRASH. A run that dies during boot prints 'Error! Failed to eval' and no announced total, no pass count, nothing. That is the SAFE half. The unsafe half is what a worker does with it: every prover, theorist and framework subagent in this project is taught to establish RED before implementing, and a boot failure looks like a failing suite. A worker that reads it as its expected RED will proceed to implement against evidence that says nothing about its test at all -- the same shape as the two defects this branch caught, where a number was true and the conclusion drawn from it was false.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN. Why it failed to boot. It did not recur: the same command passed 566 of 566 minutes later, on the same tree, with no change in between. Both dumps were moved out of the working tree to a scratchpad (they are untracked, 3.8 MB each, and one `git add -A` from being committed). erl_crash.dump is not in any .gitignore, which is a second, smaller thing worth fixing.

CLOSURE TEST. Either a reproduction that says what causes the boot failure, or -- more useful and cheaper -- the announced-total check extended so that a run producing NO announced total is reported as 'the suite did not start' rather than left for the reader to notice, plus erl_crash.dump in .gitignore.

bugs.title: Brief says to read the existing proof file, but a budget-exhausted attempt's file is parked under runs/, not Rule30/Proofs/
bugs.body: The brief for column_settledConfig_eq-2 said 'If Rule30/Proofs/ColumnSettledConfigEq.lean already exists it is a previous attempt's work: read it first'. That path did not exist. The previous attempt's complete proof was at runs/20260908T004625Z/ColumnSettledConfigEq.lean, and Rowan's commit c3d6fbe already knew it was complete. Either the brief should name the parked path when one exists, or the dispatcher should restore the parked file into Rule30/Proofs/ before starting the next attempt. bugs.resolution: d1665a3 (Fathom): prove_one now opens a run log and an attempt log at runs/<run>/<node>-<n>, the two logs run opens, so a proof file it parks lands where brief.previous_attempt_file already looks. The row read as a budget_exhausted problem; the cause was that prove-one was the only producer without an attempt directory, in every outcome. Closure test: a_file_parked_by_prove_one_is_named_by_the_next_brief_test asserts previous_attempt_file returns the parked path; watched failing first. 572 announced, 572 passed.

bugs.title: P1 worker starts with $1.85 of $4.00 already spent on the system prompt
bugs.body: The first tool result of this session reported USD budget $1.85/$4 before any work. The system prompt carries the full Vesper notebook (now very long), CLAUDE.md, the cookbook, and every served lemma's description. Under $2.20 remained for the actual attempt. bugs.title: /startup's live-guarded-sessions section is blind to a prove-one attempt, so a peer is told a live prover is an unknown session
bugs.body: /startup's LIVE GUARDED SESSIONS section exists so a hand-started session never messages a live prover, theorist or seeder mid-attempt: an arrival like that reaches the worker as an instruction from outside its brief and is recorded nowhere in its events, by construction, because an inbound message is not a tool call. It cannot see a live `prove-one` attempt at all. .claude/skills/startup/state.sh:210 globs "$runs_root"/*/*/events.jsonl, two levels deep, which is right for every producer but one: a `run` attempt writes runs/<run>/<node>-<n>/events.jsonl, a theorist runs/<run>/theorist-1/, a seeder runs/<run>/seed-1/, but `prove_one` opens one log at the run root (harness/src/harness/dispatch.gleam:89) and so writes runs/<run>/events.jsonl, one level. Confirmed on disk: runs/20260908T004625Z (prove-one) is flat; runs/20260907T195757Z (run) and runs/20260908T014245Z (theorist) both have the subdirectory. ALREADY EXERCISED, 2026-09-08 12:03Z. Keel read 'no live guarded sessions' from this section and used it to conclude that a rowless ListAgents ref was a hand-started unknown rather than a live prover, then messaged it. It was Rowan, so nothing was harmed, but the inference was invalid: this section renders 'none present' and 'none I can see' as the same output, and the startup skill's own red-flag table instructs the reader to rely on it. It is a check that says no, believed because the answer was the wanted one - the exact habit CLAUDE.md's Boundaries section names. SAME ROOT CAUSE as brief-says-to-read-the-existing-proof-file, the other reader that assumes <run>/<name>-<n>/ and so cannot find a proof file parked by prove-one; one fix closes both. The shape, in Keel's words: a write side and a read side that only meet on one of the two dispatch paths, with the tests covering the path where they meet. This row is the more expensive half - the brief costs a worker a re-proof, this costs the one guard there is against contaminating a live attempt. AN ARGUMENT THAT FAILED, recorded because it was convenient and wrong. Before settling on the write-side fix I argued that flat prove-one records exist on disk forever, so the reader must learn the run root regardless of what the writer does. `find runs -name '*.lean'` returns exactly two files: runs/20260908T004625Z/ColumnSettledConfigEq.lean, whose node is now `proved`, and runs/20260906T230339Z/isEventuallyPeriodic_of_periodic_step-2/parked-proof.lean, which predates the naming scheme and would match no reader anyway. Nothing on disk needs the root special case, so the argument for patching the readers does not survive its own evidence. FIX: prove_one opens a run log at runs/<run-id> and an attempt log at runs/<run-id>/<node>-1 the way `run` does, so one shape serves every producer and neither reader needs a special case; dispatch.gleam:1238 already notes that prove_one collapses the two logs into one. Second, and independently: the section should print its own denominator - 'no live guarded sessions (searched runs/*/*/events.jsonl)' - because even after the fix it is a glob over a layout, and a producer that does not match is invisible rather than absent. CLOSURE TEST: with a fixture whose prove-one-shaped run has a recent event and no summary.txt, STARTUP_RUNS=<fixture> bash .claude/skills/startup/state.sh lists it under LIVE GUARDED SESSIONS and prints the glob it searched; before the fix it lists nothing.
bugs.resolution: d1665a3 (Fathom): same fix — prove_one writes runs/<run>/<node>-<n>/, so state.sh's two-level glob now sees a live prove-one attempt like every other producer; and the section prints the glob it searched, so a reader can tell 'none present' from 'none I can see'. Verified live in the shared checkout at d1665a3: the section lists 20260908T123120Z/connector-1 and 20260908T124200Z/leftDiagonal_onset_le-2 and prints 'searched runs/*/*/events.jsonl'. 572 announced, 572 passed.

bugs.title: A connector can reach the network with node, and nothing on the record distinguishes that from a citation it invented
bugs.body: The connector's web fence covers WebFetch and WebSearch: every call writes a second row of kind web, at the attempt and again at completion or failure, so a failed fetch followed by a confident quote can be told apart from a real citation. That mechanism is what section 5's cite-or-mark rule rests on. But guard.gleam lets a connector Write anything under explorer/ and Bash `node explorer/<script>`, and a fetch from inside that script reaches the network without passing the hook at all. So a URL reached from a script is absent from the record, and an absent row is not evidence the connector did not fetch it. Found by review before the connector's first run. The guard cannot see inside node and widening it would not help, so 7472c13 fixed the wording rather than the fence: the brief now tells the session that a URL reached from a script is UNVERIFIED by construction, and connector_test pins that sentence. That is the honest version of the promise, not a closure of the gap. What is still open is the checking side. A captain reading a sighting cannot currently tell a cited-and-fetched claim from a cited-and-scripted one without grepping events.jsonl by hand, and nothing does that grep. The cheap version is a summary line counting web rows against the document's URLs; the honest version is accepting that node is a shell wearing a hat, as the seeder's docstring already says, and that the record covers the tools rather than the session.

bugs.title: A WebSearch writes a PreToolUse row and never a completion row, so half the web record is blind for one of the two tools
bugs.body: web_row writes a second row for every WebFetch and WebSearch PreToolUse, and for a WebFetch's PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure. The settings template registers PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure on Bash|WebFetch only. So for a WebSearch there is a row saying the search was attempted and never one saying whether it returned anything. The whole point of the second row is to tell a failed call followed by a confident citation apart from a real one, and for one of the two web tools that distinction does not exist on the record. The code matches its own docstring, which says WebFetch's PostToolUse; it does not match the design sentence 'every web call is on the record'. Found by review before the connector's first run, alongside the related gap that a web row carries event, tool, url, query and urls but no status or error field, so even a WebFetch PostToolUse row says a fetch completed without saying whether it returned the document or an error page.

bugs.title: A WebFetch whose hook body fails to decode is denied correctly and leaves no record of what was reached for
bugs.body: web_row runs only when parse_hook_input succeeded. A WebFetch whose tool_input.url arrives as a number or an object is correctly denied as Malformed and fail-closed, but the guard row is written with empty event, tool and attempted fields, and no web row is written at all. So the refusal is on the record and what the session reached for is not. This is the one denial path that leaves no trace of its target, which matters because the web record exists to be read against a document's citations: an unrecorded attempt is indistinguishable from no attempt. Found by review before the connector's first run.

bugs.title: --model and --as bind whatever follows, so a typed flag can be silently discarded in all three hand-started roles
bugs.body: parse_flags in connector.gleam, theorist.gleam and seeder.gleam all match ["--model", value, ..rest] and bind value unconditionally. So `connect --model --as Sextant` yields model="--as", vantage=Some("Sextant") and persona=None: the typed --as is silently discarded, the session runs as the eldest persona or mints one, and the bad model only surfaces at the first claude launch, after the run directory, the guard, the settings file and possibly a whole naming ceremony. A repeated --as or --model likewise takes the last one silently. This is the only way a typed flag can be lost; every other malformed input is refused by name, which was verified against real argv. Rejecting a --prefixed value would fix all three, and the three parsers are near-copies, so this belongs with each-new-session-kind-copies-the-last-ones-spine rather than being fixed three times.

bugs.title: The project keeps pairing a guard with an action that cannot wait for it, and the failure looks like a correct check
bugs.body: Four instances in two days, one family. 2026-09-08T12:26:20Z: a fast-forward of main landed fifteen seconds inside a live run, because the git status check and the git merge were issued in the same command, so the evidence that a run was live (an untracked runs/ directory and a new proof file) arrived in the same output as the action it should have prevented. Same hour: startup's live-guarded-sessions section printed 'none' and was believed, when its glob could not have seen a live prove-one attempt, so 'none present' and 'none I can see' rendered identically (see startup-cannot-see-a-live-prove-one-attempt). 2026-09-06: a killed test runner printed 193 passed and the arithmetic was sound. Same evening: a docstring said 'a runner killed between the write and the delete', which was true about everything it said while silent about assuming one runner. The common shape is not carelessness and not a wrong value. In every case the check ran, returned a well-formed result, and the result could not have changed the outcome — because it arrived too late, or measured something narrower than the reader believed, or answered a question adjacent to the one being asked. Checking harder catches none of them. Two questions do: can this check's result arrive before the thing it is meant to gate, and what was it measured over. Suggested by Fathom while reviewing the fifteen-second landing, on the grounds that filing three instances separately would lose the family. Filed as other rather than dispatch deliberately: the fix is a habit and possibly a checklist line in checkpoint, not a code change, and a row that proposes code here would be guessing.

bugs.title: connector and theorist default to fable because it was copied from the neighbouring role, so a run nobody aimed spends the scarcest allowance
bugs.body: connector.gleam:105 is `pub const default_model = "fable"`, character-identical to theorist.gleam:90; seeder.gleam:70 chose "opus". The connector's default was inherited wholesale from the nearest role rather than chosen, exactly like its 600/$80 ceilings were. On 2026-09-08 that cost the role's first-ever session: Rowan omitted --model, got fable, and the API refused the request at turn one for zero output tokens and $1.12, moving the seven-day fable window from 0.89 to 0.90 utilisation on a day when Dib's standing instruction was opus-primary because the allowance was nearly gone. Two things make this worth a row rather than a one-line edit. First, it is the same shape as the for_connector ceiling that review caught the same morning: a value nobody chose, acting at a launch site nobody can see. The difference is that the ceiling failed closed and this one spends. Second, the fix is not simply flipping the constant, because the right default differs by role and by day; what is missing is that no verb prints which model it is about to use before spending on it, and no operator-facing text says what M defaults to when --model is omitted. Filed by the author of the constant.

bugs.title: A refused request ends with CLI subtype success and reaches the summary as an ending the harness has no name for, with the discriminator in hand
bugs.body: On 2026-09-08 a connector session was refused by the API at turn one. The CLI result carried subtype `success`, and the harness summary read `ended stopped at a CLI ending this harness has no name for (result subtype success)`. The record already held the discriminator: `"type":"system","subtype":"model_refusal_no_fallback"`, `"stop_reason":"refusal"`, and `"api_refusal_category":"reasoning_extraction"`. So the harness read a refusal as an unnamed success while the reason sat one field away. Sibling of a-cli-success-result-with-no-report-is-filed-as-budget-exhausted and distinct from it: that row is a success with no report, this is a refusal wearing success. Two consequences beyond the wording. A refusal is the one ending that must not count against the ladder, because retrying the same brief at a higher rung cannot help and the ladder will spend two more attempts learning that. And a refusal is model-specific rather than a property of the brief: the same brief, vantage, guard and 56k of system context ran without refusing on opus minutes later (runs/20260908T123120Z), so a role whose default model refuses looks exactly like a broken brief until someone pays to try another model. That last is the argument for naming the ending in the summary rather than only logging it. Found by Rowan on the connector's first-ever run, runs/20260908T122952Z; framing and field names are Rowan's.
bugs.resolution: 62a3ddf (Fathom): the discriminator was closer than the row said — stop_reason: refusal sits on the SAME result event the loop already decodes, not only on the earlier model_refusal_no_fallback system event. claude.gleam decodes stop_reason now, and a refusal ends as Refused(category), a new dag.Outcome rather than a fold into HarnessFailed: the two want opposite responses, since a harness failure is a bug to fix after which the identical dispatch works, while a refusal is the model's answer to this brief and the same brief a rung up refuses again. It spends no rung (config.burns_a_rung) and scores no calibration, and because dispatch.attribute is gated on burns_a_rung it also cannot be re-labelled HarnessFailed — that fell out rather than being designed, and was checked rather than assumed. Named where humans read: seeder.ended_words and theorist.ended_words (the compiler found both), and refused=<model> in dispatch.rungs_tried, which it needed because a refusal appeared in neither failed= nor harness= and left no trace on a status row at all. HAZARD FOR READERS: dag.outcome_from_string ends _ -> Error(Nil), so once a refused lands in blueprint/dag.json a harness built from source predating 62a3ddf cannot read the board at all — not a node with an odd word, a board that fails to load. Rowan's call was to land it and not soften the decoder; rebase stale worktrees. Nothing contains refused until a real refusal happens. Suite 649/649, exit 0.

bugs.title: A captain holding direct evidence about a node's difficulty has no field for it, so the record keeps the harness's weaker inference
bugs.body: Worked instance, 2026-09-08. `leftDiagonal_shift_of_white` was seeded from a proof that already compiles: `explorer/scratch_whitestep.lean` proves it in six lines -- `leftDiagonal_recurrence` rewritten at two white cells and a Bool case split, no induction. It is the easiest of the five nodes seeded from crystals 45 and 53. It came back `budget_exhausted` on haiku at 41 turns and $0.67, while `leftDiagonal_black_after_white`, which genuinely needs a `Nat.le_induction`, closed on the same model in 12 turns. So the node's durable record now reads as the hard one of the batch and the actual hard one reads as easy. NOT the closed row `a-failed-bottom-rung-is-not-evidence-about-the-node`: Keel checked that one's fix rather than recalling it, and every reader it named is handled -- the `model` field sits in the attempt beside the outcome, `roster.tally` scores calibration only for an attempt that closed a node or ran on the top rung so this failure moves no figure, and the status row appends `failed=haiku`. The ladder spending a cheap rung is the ladder working. The residue is different and is about evidence the harness does not have: the captain KNOWS this node is easy, because a working proof of it exists in the checkout, and there is no field on the node to say so. `description` carries it as prose that nothing reads as a difficulty signal, and the seeded descriptions for these five did name the scratch file and its line count -- so the information was written down and still did not reach the reader. The harness's evidence, '41 turns on haiku', is exactly what a genuinely hard S node looks like at that rung, so the two cases are indistinguishable in the record while being distinguishable in fact. When the node closes at the next rung the scratch proof will look redundant, and nobody will learn that it was the thing that made the 41 turns legible. Suggested shape, not a demand: a field on the node for external warrant -- a path to a proof that already compiles, or a kernel-checked scratch file -- that the status table and a theorist's brief can read, so a captain's stronger evidence outranks the harness's weaker inference instead of being buried beside it. Reframed from Rowan's first version by Keel, which was wrong about the `model` field being absent.

bugs.title: A second gleam run beside a live run is a designed shape, and the shared build directory makes it unsafe for one window after a landing
bugs.body:
CLAUDE.md says a seeder's guard sits on the run port base plus 100 'so it can run beside a live run', and the theorist (+200) and connector (+300) families say the same. So a second `gleam run` in the shared checkout beside a live one is a designed shape, and the port families are spaced for exactly that. Nothing separates `harness/build/`, which all of them share. Measured by Fathom in its own worktree, `harness@dispatch.beam` mtime to the nanosecond: (1) no-op `gleam build` with the tree unchanged -- 'Compiled in 0.10s', beam mtime UNCHANGED; (2) `touch src/harness/dispatch.gleam` then build -- 'Compiled in 0.10s', beam mtime STILL UNCHANGED, because Gleam hashes content rather than mtimes; (3) append one comment line then build -- 'Compiled in 0.73s', beam mtime MOVED. So the trigger is neither an invocation nor a landing: it is a landing that changes the CONTENT of Gleam source under harness/. A landing that moves only agents/, blueprint/, docs/ or .claude/ opens no window at all, which matters because a rule phrased as 'after every landing' would make people serialise landings that cost nothing. Why a mid-run rewrite bites is reasoning rather than measurement and should be read as such: the running BEAM has its modules already loaded and replacing a .beam on disk does not disturb those, but it does disturb modules loaded AFTER the rewrite -- Erlang loads lazily, so a dispatcher that first touches `seed` at the end of a run, or `bugs` when a signal is auto-filed, picks up new code in the middle of an attempt whose other modules are old. A mixed-version run rather than a crash, which is the worse failure because it looks like nothing. Hit on 2026-09-08 with three hand-started sessions in one checkout: Keel landing the connector, Fathom landing a prove-one fix, and Rowan wanting a connector session and a prover run concurrently. Worked around by sequencing -- finish the run, land, one quiet `gleam build`, then start the next session -- which removes the window entirely. Filed as documentation-and-sequencing rather than code: the fix is most likely a sentence in CLAUDE.md next to the port-family paragraph, saying that the ports are separated and the build directory is not, and that the quiet moment to land is between sessions.

--- AMENDED 2026-09-08T21:18Z by Rowan, who filed it ---

The claim above is too blunt and I acted on it wrongly today, holding a peer's landing for half an hour on it. The mechanism is narrower.

Erlang loads a module on first call and never reloads it on its own. So a recompile into the shared build/ can only affect a live node through a module the node has NOT YET CALLED. Three cases, not one:

1. Module not in the live node's import graph at all -- always safe. Keel's first landing changed only dispatch.gleam, which connector.gleam does not import, so it could not have reached my session under any circumstances.
2. Module in the graph and already loaded -- safe. Keel's second landing (c60e411) changed guard.gleam, which IS imported by connector, theorist and prover; but guard.start runs before the first turn, so the module was loaded. Tested rather than argued: the recompile took 1.08s against the usual 0.09s and all three live sessions survived it, checked by pid rather than by port alone.
3. Module in the graph whose FIRST call comes at session end -- the real hazard, and the one this row failed to name. The report-writing and roster-writing path is exactly that shape. It is the worst possible place for it, because the session's own record is what breaks, at the moment it is written, after everything has already been spent.

So the rule to apply is "already-loaded beats in-graph", and the question to ask before a rebuild beside a live session is not "did something land" but "is any module this node has yet to call among the ones that changed". A row that says "unsafe for one window after a landing" makes people hold for landings that cannot touch them (as I did) while saying nothing about the case that can.

bugs.title: A running session rewrites the scripts other sessions are quoting, and neither reproducing the number nor reading the source detects it
bugs.body: On 2026-09-08 a live connector iterated on explorer/portage_odometer.mjs and explorer/portage_pairmap.mjs while two other sessions read and re-ran them. Three figures moved under us: a settled-term count 1280 -> 479.7, two profinite commuting rates 0.138/0.396 -> 0.149/0.407, and an internal consistency counter 0/12/252 -> 0/0/0 when the connector fixed a real bug in the same window one of us was reasoning about it. Both of us defended against staleness in the ways that feel sufficient and neither works. Keel re-ran the script rather than trusting the peer message, and reported the result as 'independently reproduced' without naming the version, which is true and unfalsifiable as stated. Rowan re-read the source and re-ran it an hour later and got a different value for the same quantity. Care is demonstrably not the fix, because care is what both were exercising. One of the misses had a second and distinct mechanism worth recording separately: a profinite figure was missed not because it had moved but because the re-run was piped through `head -8` and the line was the ninth, so a window was chosen and not stated. Every load-bearing claim survived and only decorative figures moved, which is luck rather than method. Two fixes, both cheap. Quote every computed figure as `value @ sha1` of the script that produced it, taken before and after the run so a mid-run rewrite is visible. And re-run once when the authoring session is down, quoting only pinned figures in anything a captain or Dib reads. Related to a-check-whose-result-cannot-precede-the-action-is-not-a-check: same family, different limb -- there the check could not arrive in time, here the thing being measured moves while it is measured.

bugs.title: A spend is authorised in dollars whose denomination is invisible: the dispatch surface never says which model
bugs.body: A captain authorising an attempt sees a dollar ceiling and never the model, so $20 of the scarcest allowance is indistinguishable from $20 of the plentiful one at the moment of the decision. Worked instance, 2026-09-08, and the sentence that names it is the captain's own: 'I told Dib the attempt would cost about $20 and did not say what it would be spent on, because I did not check -- I knew the budget and not the model.' Dib had asked that day for fable to be protected (allowance at 90 percent, two days from reset) and everyone was on opus by instruction. Three separate paths spent fable anyway, all of them without the spender seeing it: (1) `gleam run -- connect` with no --model, refused at turn 1 on fable, $1.12 for zero output tokens; (2) the research rung -- `leftDiagonal_onset_le` second attempt, Selvage on fable, 5 turns, $10.29, abandoned, seven_day_overage_included utilization 0.90 -> 0.92 across that one attempt; (3) `theorise` carries the same default and would have been the third had it not been passed --model explicitly after the first two. NOT the same defect as `a-role-default-model-is-inherited-and-spends-the-scarcest-budget`, which is about `connector.default_model = "fable"` being character-identical to theorist.gleam:90 -- a constant copied from a neighbouring role that nobody chose for the role it now governs; its fix is to choose the constant. And NOT a defect in the ladder: config.gleam:156-163 reads S -> [haiku, sonnet, opus, fable], M -> [sonnet, opus, fable], L -> [opus, fable], documented as 'cheapest first, ending on the strongest model the CLI offers', with on_research_rung (config.gleam:191-195) firing once failed_attempts reaches len(ladder)-1. That ordering is deliberate and correct; a research node SHOULD end at the strongest model. The defect is that the ordering is invisible where it is paid for. What the three instances share, and the only thing they share, is a spend whose denomination is not stated at the point of authorisation. Suggested shape, not a demand: name the model wherever a spend is announced or authorised -- the run summary's cost line, the status table's per-attempt row, and above all the captain-facing dispatch line, so that 'this attempt may cost $20' reads as 'this attempt may cost $20 of fable'. A dollar figure with an unstated currency is the same class as a count with an unstated denominator, which this board already has several rows about; see `a-live-sessions-computed-numbers-are-quoted-as-settled` and `a-check-whose-result-cannot-precede-the-action-is-not-a-check`. Distinction drawn by Keel, who declined to fold it into its own row and was right to.
